title: Orbital Guard: circuit mapping and safe rollout for batching/caching cost ops
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build an end-to-end "orbital guard" runbook and implementation for applying automated batching and KV-prefetch caching recommendations while guaranteeing latency/throughput SLOs. The feature must provide adaptive limiters, SLO-aware routing for canaries, multi-signal anomaly detection, and deterministic rollback triggers so cost-saving configuration changes can be applied automatically and safely across Hosted and Dedicated deployments.
background: We already have recommenders that suggest batching and caching profiles, and command-and-control for staged rollouts. Customers want more automated ops: apply recommendations safely and recover without manual intervention when regressions occur. Existing tickets implemented pieces of this (adaptive batching advisors, staged apply playbooks), but there is no single orchestrator that maps config changes to safety circuits, ties telemetry to rollback logic, and exposes a deterministic policy for routing/limiting during experiments.
acceptance_criteria: 1) The orbital guard service can ingest a batching/caching recommendation payload and synthesize a rollout plan with canary cohorts and traffic splits. 2) For each rollout, SLO predicates (p95 latency and tokens/sec throughput) are evaluated in real-time and compared against dynamic baselines. 3) If anomaly detectors trigger, the system performs a safe rollback or progressive throttling according to policy. 4) Operators can override via Console immediately and see a decomposition of cost delta vs observed SLO delta. 5) End-to-end integration tests simulate noisy traffic and validate rollback within the configured SLA window.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (API/modeling): define the canonical recommendation schema and a 'circuit map' that binds config diffs to safety circuits. Implement a stateless planner that emits staged rollout steps (cohorts, traffic percents, limiter settings). Phase 2 (runtime): extend the runtime control plane with SLO-aware router hooks and a lightweight limiter service that can enforce per-cohort qps/tokens and prefetch budgets. Phase 3 (detection and orchestration): ship anomaly detectors (baseline drift + Z-score over p95/p99 + throughput delta by cohort) and the orchestrator that listens to detectors and executes rollback/throttle actions. Phase 4 (Console + runbook): surface rollouts, allow manual abort/override, and build analytics for cost vs SLO tradeoffs. Each phase includes backwards-compatible feature flags.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal feature-flagged rollout to canary workspace with synthetic traffic (2 weeks). 2) Enable on low-risk customer tenants with strict p95 guardrails and low QPS (2 weeks). 3) Expand cohorts incrementally by doubling traffic each step up to target, with automated rollback check at each step. 4) Gradual ramp to 100% for tenants that pass all checks (monitored for 48h). 5) Post-rollout review and metrics audit. All steps must provide immediate abort and automatic rollback on failure.
monitoring_and_alerting: Primary SLO metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, server-side tokens/sec (throughput), error rate, queue depth, tail-kv-hit-rate for prefetched keys. Anomaly signals: 1) statistical drift: rolling Z-score > 3 for p95 compared to 1h baseline, 2) step drop in throughput > 15% sustained for 2 consecutive 30s windows, 3) error rate spike > 0.5% absolute. Alerts: critical pager on auto-rollback, warning slack channel for cohort drift, dashboard widget with cohort timelines and cost delta estimate. Link to dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/opt-orbital-guard (placeholder).
test_plan: Unit tests for planner and limiter logic. Integration harness that replays production traces with variable sequence lengths and failure modes. Chaos tests: inject delayed responses and transient GPU OOMs to verify graceful throttling and rollback. End-to-end smoke with canary cohort verifying rollback within 90s of trigger. Include perf benchmarks showing no added median latency overhead beyond 1-3ms at p95 under normal operation.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: False positives in anomaly detectors causing unnecessary rollbacks and lost savings. Mitigation: combine multiple signals (latency + throughput + error) and require consensus of two detectors or one detector + threshold breach. Risk: throttling may cascade across upstream services. Mitigation: limiter is workload-aware and uses token-bucket with backoff policies; add circuit isolation for critical routes. Risk: incompatible cached state between model variants. Mitigation: require cache warm-up window in plan and fall back to no-cache variant if mismatch detected.
open_questions: 1) Should rollback be immediate full revert or progressive backoff? (proposal: immediate revert for fatal signals, progressive for soft regressions). 2) What is the canonical baseline window to compute dynamic SLO thresholds? (proposal: configurable 1h default, with min 15m). 3) How to surface multi-tenant impact for Shared Dedicated pools? Need cross-tenant isolation policies.
notes: - Work should be cross-functional with Console, Runtime, and Reliability teams. - Coordinate with Customer Success for early adopters. - Use existing batching/caching recommender outputs (schema v2) as input. - PR checklist will include integration test recordings and dashboard snapshots.
